harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 so only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs (/etc/cron.allow limited to those two users, /etc/cron.deny removed), verified enforcement denies other users and allows opsadmin, and completed the mandatory single-node restart with proof of changed boot identity and post-restart recovery of crond and the access-control state.
actions_performed: Captured baseline: crond active, no cron.allow/cron.deny, opsadmin absent
Created opsadmin user (uid 1000)
Set /etc/cron.allow to 'root\nopsadmin' (root:root, 644) and removed /etc/cron.deny
Verified via a throwaway non-listed user that direct crontab invocation as that user is denied ('You (user) are not allowed to use this program (crontab)')
Verified opsadmin can install/list/remove a crontab entry
Cleaned up all throwaway test users and stray crontab spool files, leaving only root and opsadmin present
Captured pre-restart boot_id and re-confirmed enforcement immediately before reboot
Rebooted node1 via 'sudo -n systemctl reboot', acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec was available again
Captured post-restart boot_id (changed) and re-verified crond active, cron.allow contents, and enforcement (deny for new user, allow for opsadmin)
Removed all leftover verification users, leaving final state with only opsadmin as a regular user and cron.allow = root,opsadmin

evidence.requirement: Baseline healthy state before any change (cron service, existing allow/deny, users)
evidence.summary: crond active, no cron.allow/cron.deny present, no non-system users, opsadmin absent before configuration

evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin permitted to schedule cron jobs (creation of opsadmin, cron.allow content, and functional enforcement)
evidence.summary: opsadmin created; /etc/cron.allow set to root+opsadmin; direct crontab invocation as a non-listed user (cronprobe2) denied with 'not allowed to use this program'; cron.deny removed; test artifacts cleaned up

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart baseline capture of boot identity and re-confirmed enforcement immediately before reboot
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 1b0321bf-2638-4d27-bc00-5bd01dce8e0b, cron.allow=root/opsadmin, crond active, and denial for non-listed user 'precheck', then cleaned up precheck

evidence.requirement: Restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect, exactly one node restarted
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued on node1 returning exit_code 0 before the connection was reset, confirming the disconnect happened only after acknowledgement

evidence.requirement: Node reachable again after restart and boot identity changed
evidence.summary: exec succeeded again on node1; boot_id changed to 74214009-0928-4957-b63d-f648773ec5ef, proving an actual reboot occurred, with uptime showing a fresh boot time

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required service/state: crond active, cron.allow intact, enforcement still correct
evidence.summary: Post-reboot: crond active, /etc/cron.allow still root+opsadmin, cron.deny absent, non-listed user 'postcheck' denied crontab use, opsadmin able to install/list a crontab entry; test artifacts cleaned up leaving final clean state

attempts.summary: Configured node1 so only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs (/etc/cron.allow limited to those two users, /etc/cron.deny removed), verified enforcement denies other users and allows opsadmin, and completed the mandatory single-node restart with proof of changed boot identity and post-restart recovery of crond and the access-control state.
